audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline play is backwards. It says four separate times to 'ramp Shield of Durand into his Null Sphere, eat the silence on the channel, then release the taunt'. Null Sphere does not silence, and it is specifically the thing that ends that channel.
audit.why: Riot's Null Sphere text: 'Kassadin fires an orb of void energy at a target, dealing damage and INTERRUPTING CHANNELS. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' No silence anywhere. Channel interruption means a Null Sphere thrown at a charging Galio cancels Shield of Durand before the taunt ever fires — so charging W into his Q is the single worst thing a Galio can do here, and the page recommends it as the win condition.
audit.corrected: Inverted across both layers: bait Null Sphere first (9s at rank 1), then start the W charge. The 'silence' wording is gone; the don't and Common Mistakes now name charging into his Q as the mistake.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire full layer is built on 'trade on the Riftwalk cooldown' — tldr, winCon, every phase why, the cooldown block, the do's, the trading rules and the loading tip.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds. There is no cooldown window; at rank 3 he blinks every two seconds. Riot's own text says the limiter is cost: 'Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana.' The thing to track is his mana bar, not a timer, and Nether Blade (7s) is how he refills it.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block, do's line, tldr and winCon rewritten around mana as the limiter, with Riftwalk's real 5s/2s numbers stated so the reader stops waiting for a window that never comes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse is mentioned once as part of 'burst', with nothing about how he gets it.
audit.why: Riot: 'Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up, Kassadin can use Force Pulse.' Your own casts charge it. A Galio spamming Winds of War next to him is loading the cone that slows him out of your Justice Punch — that changes how you poke a shoved wave, and it was nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Written into the first-item spike, the early text and whys[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone is called an 'anti-AP passive barrier', which is not what it is, and the full layer's level-6 phase says 'Reassess his ultimate too'.
audit.why: Void Stone is not a barrier: 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' It is flat magic-damage reduction against a champion whose whole kit is magic, plus the ability to walk through minions — so the wave never blocks his approach or his escape. Riftwalk at 6 is the spike, and it is a 500-range blink.
audit.corrected: Void Stone named correctly in the early text and the level-1 phase, including the unit-collision half; Riftwalk's 500 range noted at the level-6 phase.

audit.whatIsWrong: The loading tip ends with 'Anti-heal if he sustains'.
audit.why: Kassadin has no heal in his kit — no heal flag on any ability, and no lifesteal component. The line is dead space on a loading screen that should be carrying the Null Sphere rule instead.

edits.before: Kassadin is a melee farmer for the first three levels and you abuse exactly that. Chip him with Winds of War tornadoes from range — his anti-AP passive barrier and Null Sphere shield only soak so much, and he has no Riftwalk to disengage. The trap to dodge: don't throw Justice Punch in blind, because his Null Sphere can silence you out of casting it and the shield blanks the first hit anyway. Hold Shield of Durand instead: when he steps up to last-hit and throws Q, ramp the channel, eat the silence on the shield, then release the taunt into a Justice Punch knockup for a clean trade he can't answer.
edits.after: Kassadin is a melee farmer for the first three levels and you abuse exactly that. Chip him with Winds of War from range — though Void Stone gives him flat magic reduction and lets him walk through your wave, so minions never block him. The trap: do NOT start the W charge while he still holds Null Sphere. It interrupts channels, so his Q cancels Shield of Durand before the taunt ever fires. Bait it — 9s at rank 1 — then charge, release the taunt, and punch the knockup. Watch your own casting too: every spell you throw near him charges his Force Pulse.

edits.before: This is your takeover window and the whole reason this lane is 60%. At 6, Hero's Entrance is a taunt-lock all-in that ruins a pre-Riftwalk, pre-items Kassadin — and if he plays safe, you just R another lane and snowball the map while he farms. His Null Sphere shield and pre-Rod burst can't out-trade your Shield of Durand damage reduction, which is amplified hard against his all-magic kit, so every time he commits Q into you it refunds onto your shield, not his health bar. Bait the silence, taunt, Justice Punch knockup, walk away ahead. Keep him under your tower and deny stacks.
edits.after: This is your takeover window and the whole reason this lane reads 60%. At 6, Hero's Entrance is a taunt-lock all-in that ruins a pre-items Kassadin — and if he plays safe, you R another lane and snowball the map while he farms. His Null Sphere shield and pre-Rod burst can't out-trade Shield of Durand's reduction, which is amplified hard against his all-magic kit. The sequencing is the whole matchup: his Null Sphere interrupts channels and cancels your charge, so spend his Q first, then charge, taunt, punch, and walk away ahead. Keep him under tower and deny stacks.

edits.before: Be honest: Kassadin is the textbook hard scaler and 2+ items is his window, not yours. Once he has Rod of Ages and Lich Bane online, Riftwalk lets him blink in and out of your Justice Punch and taunt range, kite your short engage, and burst a squishy before Shield of Durand even finishes channeling. Your damage and tankiness plateau while his per-blink output keeps climbing. So your job is to make late game irrelevant — end the lane and the map on your 6-and-first-item lead, and in fights group to taunt-peel for your carries rather than dueling him solo.
edits.after: Be honest: Kassadin is the textbook hard scaler and 2+ items is his window. Once Rod of Ages and Lich Bane are online, Riftwalk is a 500-range blink on a 2-second cooldown at rank 3 — there is no timer to wait out, only his mana bar, and Nether Blade refills that every 7 seconds off an auto. He kites your short engage and bursts a squishy before your channel finishes. So make late game irrelevant: end on your 6-and-first-item lead, and in fights group to taunt-peel for your carries rather than duelling him.

notes: This page had its central play inverted. Both layers told the reader to 'ramp Shield of Durand into his Null Sphere and eat the silence on the channel'. Null Sphere has no silence in Riot's current text — what it does is 'interrupting channels', which means throwing it at a charging Galio CANCELS Shield of Durand before the taunt fires. The recommended combo was the exact thing that loses the trade. Everything now sequences the other way: spend his Q (9s at rank 1) first, then charge. Second structural problem: the whole full layer was framed as 'trade on the Riftwalk cooldown'. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds — at rank 3 he blinks every two seconds, so no such window exists; Riot's text says the real limiter is escalating mana cost, and Nether Blade (7s) refunds mana on an auto. I retargeted the tracking advice to his mana bar but left focus.text as 'Kassadin Riftwalk', since focus.text is 17 characters and no accurate replacement fits inside +/-10%. Third: Force Pulse charges from spells cast in his vicinity — including yours — so poking a shoved wave next to him loads the cone he slows you with. Fourth: Void Stone is flat magic-damage reduction plus unit-collision immunity, not a 'barrier', so your wave never blocks him. NOT WRITTEN: _missing-interactions.json says 'Galio can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Shield of Durand (W)' — that comes from a derived 'channel' flag on Null Sphere, which exists only because the word 'channels' appears in its description. Null Sphere is not itself a channel, so I did not write that claim. Sample here is small: 45 games at 60%.
